formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature, the signer (owner) lets `spender` spend up to `value` wstETH from the signer's balance. The allowance replaces any earlier one.
The permit is accepted only until `deadline` (block.timestamp <= deadline). It uses up the owner's current nonce.
formats.shown: The intent is "Authorize spending of tokens". The fields show the spender as a raw address, the max amount in wstETH (or "Unlimited" at 2^255 and above), the valid-until date and the owner.

findings.title: Permit has no test case, so the wstETH amount and the Unlimited threshold are never exercised.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: "cases: 0 (no tx)". The `value` field in descriptor.json uses tokenPath "@.to" and threshold 0x8000…0000 with the message "Unlimited".
findings.fix: Add an EIP-712 test with domain name "Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0", version "1", chainId 59144 and verifyingContract 0xB5beDd42000b71FddE22D3eE8a79Bd49A568fC8F. Include one finite value and one value at or above 2^255.

findings.title: Permit domain name comes from proxy storage; the source shows it but cannot confirm the current value.
findings.evidence: EIP712Upgradeable._EIP712Name returns the stored `_name`, which `initialize`/`initializeV2` set through __ERC20Permit_init(_tokenName). The proxy constructor data shows initialize("Wrapped liquid staked Ether 2.0","wstETH",18). That matches the descriptor domain name, and version "1" matches.
